speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Programme; Brieskorn links and exotic spheres
summary: The actual opening heading and programme occupy P000140: statistical mechanics, pseudodifferential operators, algebraic groups, and deformations. A report attributed to Hirzebruch then describes exotic spheres as links of isolated hypersurface singularities. The catalogue range overlaps subsequent talks; items below follow the handwritten headings. The printed exponent requires an emendation, not merely removal of an uncertainty marker.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Bass rigidity and an integral cohomology reduction
summary: P000141--P000142 report Bass’s work on rigidity of \(\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)\), relating deformations to first cohomology and proposing reduction modulo a prime. This resumes the cohomological rigidity and congruence-subgroup discussions indexed at 1964-8.1--2 and 1964-24.1--2. The established conclusion and the incompletely recorded proof reduction must be distinguished.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Anosov systems, structural stability, and Smale questions
summary: The handwritten Arnold heading is on P000142; his discussion ends on P000145. Uniform hyperbolicity, an arithmetic nilmanifold, Morse--Smale systems, Axiom A, and spectral decomposition are interspersed with explicit conjectures. Positive and negative later answers belong to different questions; in particular hyperbolicity of the nonwandering set alone does not force dense periodic points.

speaker: G. E. Shilov
title: Regular Hilbert-space functions and a first-order mean operator
summary: P000146--P000147 introduce a uniform algebra between weak and norm continuity, limiting finite-dimensional spherical means, and a mean-defined differential operator. Linear boundary problems and a fixed-point approach to a semilinear equation follow. Shilov’s 1967 papers closely match this announcement, but the operator is not the usual Hilbert-space trace Laplacian.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Uniqueness, admissibility, and viscosity for hyperbolic systems
summary: The middle and lower parts of P000147 ask when nonlinear first-order systems have unique solutions. Scalar convexity, characteristic eigenvector curves, conservation form, viscosity, and travelling waves are juxtaposed. The equations and solution classes in the hydrodynamic remarks are too incomplete for an exact publication match.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: The representation-ring completion theorem and the circle
summary: P000148 explicitly reports part of what Atiyah had explained. The augmentation-ideal completion theorem is illustrated by \(S^1\) and \(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}\). Two literal slips deserve separate treatment: calling the uncompleted map an embedding for every compact group, and giving the wrong fibre and total space for the tautological bundle.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Equivariant completion, induction, and a noncompact programme
summary: P000149--P000150 continue Atiyah’s programme: skeletal limits, equivariant vector bundles, the Borel construction, and reductions to a unitary group and maximal torus. Gelfand asks for a noncompact analogue and suggests a Plancherel replacement for dimension, but does not specify a representation ring or ideal. The family-index explanation is continued at record 104.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Canonical ensembles and factorial correlation functions
summary: The first lecture starts at P000151 and ends near the top of P000155. It defines continuum and lattice models, the thermodynamic limit, canonical Gibbs weights, and correlation densities. The 1968 lectures explicitly identify the autumn 1966 Gelfand seminar as a source, while tracing the earlier course to Khumsan in September 1965. Much of this first lecture is foundational exposition, not a new result. The ordered-pair convention is retained consistently.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Bulk correlations, clustering, and representative means
summary: The second lecture begins midway down P000155 and ends on P000157. It deliberately labels several thermodynamic assertions as hypotheses, allows an effective specific volume depending on the correlation order, and uses clustering to argue that pair observables concentrate. The 1968 version restores an integrable decay requirement; nevertheless the displayed variance proof needs more than the stated \(L^1\) condition on the pair kernel. Our bounded development isolates the exact probabilistic implication and its limits.

speaker: D. A. Kazhdan
title: Isolation of the trivial representation and lattice finiteness
summary: Two finiteness conclusions for lattices are announced on P000158, followed by the representation-theoretic mechanism now called property \(T\). Kazhdan’s short paper, received two weeks after the seminar, is an unusually close match. A separate sentence about groups over \(\mathbb Q\) retains no conclusion and cannot be identified with a theorem.

speaker: Lee Lorch
title: Higher monotonicity of zeros and wave integrals
summary: The lecturer’s handwritten name on P000158 is uncertain; the MCCME entry and the joint work with Peter Szego identify Lee Lorch. The page treats Sturm comparison, higher finite differences of zeros, Bessel and Airy examples, and integrals between consecutive zeros. The strict inequality cannot follow from the weak derivative hypotheses exactly as written. Gelfand’s endpoint remark is mathematically suggestive but not completely recorded.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: A recapitulation of equivariant K-theory and completion
summary: On P000159 Gelfand explicitly repeats Bernstein’s and Atiyah’s material: equivariant bundles, the Borel construction, the representation-ring action, and the approximate identification with ordinary K-theory. These are new notebook occurrences of the same constructions, not additional discovery claims.

speaker: I. N. Bernstein
title: Families of elliptic operators and the index bundle
summary: P000159--P000160 supply the analytic construction behind the K-theoretic direct image, then a finite-dimensional modification of a Fredholm family. The essential issue is that kernel dimensions jump. The index is a virtual bundle after stabilization, not generally the difference of two pre-existing kernel and cokernel bundles. This continues 1964-15.4.

speaker: Louis Nirenberg
title: Complex powers and an analytic index formula
summary: The actual notes occupy P000161--P000162, after the preceding talk on P000160. Nirenberg reports Seeley's and H\"ormander's analytic approach to the index: positive-spectrum cancellation, complex powers, continuation of kernels and a local expression at exponent zero. Gelfand comments on analytic descriptions of topological quantities. The catalogue's wider interval also contains Minlos's next lecture. Both formula-critical pages were inspected against their scans and Seeley's contemporary preprint in its published Russian translation \citep[pp.~96--98]{seeley1968powers}.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Infinite configurations and correlation axioms
summary: The actual lecture is P000163--P000164. It constructs the measurable space of locally finite configurations, discusses limiting Gibbs measures and mixing, invokes ergodicity for mean density and introduces thermodynamic functions. Gelfand asks for intrinsic axioms on correlations. Minlos's expanded lectures trace their first delivery to Khumsan in September 1965 and their amplification to the autumn 1966 Gelfand seminar \citep[pp.~137--138]{minlos1968lectures}. That publication distinguishes results and hypotheses more carefully than this notebook.

speaker: R. A. Minlos
title: Energy, wall pressure and entropy
summary: The fourth lecture occupies the upper part of P000165. It records the energy derivative, a separate moving-wall pressure conjecture, and entropy per particle. The manuscript itself has an entropy sign error and an erroneous reciprocal-temperature factor. Arnold starts below the separator. The expanded treatment is \citet[Lecture IV]{minlos1968lectures}.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Lagrangian planes and the Maslov class
summary: Arnold begins in lower P000165 and continues through P000166. He identifies \(\Lambda(n)=U(n)/O(n)\), constructs determinant squared and pulls the circle class back by the tangent map of a Lagrangian manifold. The exact authorial match is \citet{arnold1967characteristic}, submitted 28 September 1966, before this talk, and published January 1967. It clarifies the geometric class behind earlier occurrence 1964-21.3.

speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Recovering a compact group from tensor intertwiners
summary: The actual report is the upper-middle portion of P000167. Gelfand explains reconstruction from irreducible representation spaces and their tensor intertwiners. Multiplicities alone and arbitrary matrix solutions require corrections. The top of the same page separately says “Minlos, Lecture 5: Phase transitions”, with no mathematical content following that heading; no additional MCCME record or phase-transition theorem is invented. Nirenberg's heat-kernel report below belongs to record 110.

speaker: Louis Nirenberg
title: Varadhan's short-time heat-kernel asymptotic
summary: The lower portion of P000167 records Nirenberg reporting Varadhan's result: the leading exponential of the heat kernel measures squared geodesic distance. The handwritten general formula omits the factor four that is present in its own Euclidean example. A final allusion to elliptic eigenvalues contains no identifiable theorem. The close publication is \citet{varadhan1967fundamental}, published in May 1967.

speaker: M. I. Vishik
title: Pseudodifferential operators: two lecture headings
summary: At the top of P000168, Vishik's first lecture has only “I. Kohn--Nirenberg definition” and “II. Boundedness theorem”. No hypotheses, formulas or proof survive. A separate unindexed heading attributes a Sturm--Liouville topic to a professor whose surname is uncertain (possibly Lorch); it has no mathematical statement either. The entries below distinguish contextual reconstructions from actual recorded assertions.

speaker: M. I. Vishik
title: Composition and formal symbols
summary: Vishik's second lecture begins on P000168 and ends in the upper half of P000169. Unlike the preceding outline, it supplies the composition expansion, its Fourier/Taylor proof, formal asymptotic symbols, uniqueness modulo smoothing and realization of a formal symbol. These are expository parts of the calculus already published in 1965 by Kohn--Nirenberg and H\"ormander \citep{kohnnirenberg1965algebra,hormander1965pseudo}. Oleinik begins below and belongs to record 113.

speaker: O. A. Oleinik
title: The unsteady Prandtl boundary layer
summary: Oleinik begins in lower P000169 and finishes P000170. She contrasts viscous and ideal-fluid boundary conditions, writes the Prandtl system and data, and announces uniqueness, short-time existence, existence near the inflow for all time, and stability. The monotonicity and compatibility assumptions needed for her theorems are absent from the notebook. The announcement had already appeared in 1966 \citep{oleinik1966system}; the detailed later treatment is \citet[Lecture II, Theorems 4--5]{oleinik1968boundary}.

speaker: M. S. Agranovich
title: Pseudodifferential heading and nine geometry problems
summary: P000171 begins “Agranovich, Lecture 3 on pseudodifferential operators”, but no mathematical exposition of that lecture follows. Instead P000171--P000172 contain a numbered differential-geometry problem list, without an explicit speaker attribution for the list. It includes Helgason's spherical support question, entire Monge--Ampere and minimal-graph problems, metric reconstruction, symmetric-space eigenfunctions, infinite volume, two geodesic questions and contact structures. These are associated with this record by manuscript position, not individually attributed to Agranovich. P000173 begins Arnold's following record and is excluded.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Singularities of smooth mappings I: stability, jets, and Boardman strata
summary: The first lecture moves from Morse and Whitney models through the perturbation \(z^2+\varepsilon\bar z\), smooth moduli, and Thom\textquotesingle s topological announcement to jets, transversality, and Boardman\textquotesingle s universal strata. It resumes the earlier 1965 record 72, including GP-1965-03. Arnold\textquotesingle s 1968 survey explicitly derives from his 1966 lectures and supplies unusually close publication matches. The MCCME catalogue associates P000172--P000180 with the record; the actual dated lecture starts on P000173 and ends on P000178.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Singularities of smooth mappings II: intrinsic derivatives and local algebras
summary: The second lecture constructs Boardman ideals, states their codimension formula, and studies Morin germs and intrinsic quadratic pencils. It then explains the first smooth moduli, Mather\textquotesingle s local-algebra and infinitesimal-stability criteria, smooth preparation, and five real corank-two families. The scans reveal substantive mathematical slips in the codimension conventions and one mixed monomial; the corrected statements are separated from the notebook readings. The MCCME catalogue span P000178--P000188 overlaps both adjacent records; the dated lecture itself occupies P000179--P000186.

title: Year 1967
summary: This is the MCCME catalogue\textquotesingle s year-heading record, not a separate mathematical lecture. Its broad page interval overlaps the end of Arnold\textquotesingle s lecture and the February plan. P000186 ends with a next-meeting notice for 13 February 1967. No distinct theorem, problem, or construction is assigned to the heading.

title: Plan for 13 February 1967
summary: The catalogue labels the record 13-Feb-67 but supplies no machine-readable date; the label is preserved as a title. The plan lists Kirillov on Harish-Chandra (about ten lectures), Anosov on Maslov and semiclassics (two), Kazhdan on A.~Weil (six or seven), Dynin on the index (three), Anosov on first-order Pfaff equations (one), and Bernstein on the \(KG\)-functor (two). The next meeting is assigned to Kirillov and Anosov. The Russian surname \ru{Дынин} is Dynin, not the English translation\textquotesingle s Dynkin. These are topic announcements without mathematical assertions, so the plan has no occurrence-index items. The catalogue span P000186--P000188 is wider than the plan at the top of P000187.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Invariant eigendistributions and the first descent construction
summary: The first lecture on Harish-Chandra begins after the programme on P000187. It states local integrability and regular-set analyticity for conjugation-invariant, centrally finite distributions, then sketches ellipticity, descent through centralizers, and reduction near the identity to the Lie algebra. Gelfand supplies explicit central operators for the general linear group. The lecture ends on P000191 before Dynin's heading. Several compressed proof steps need correction; the unexplained sentence about characters at infinity is retained as unidentified.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Pseudodifferential operators on bundles and the de Rham example
summary: Dynin begins after Kirillov on P000191, globalizing pseudodifferential operators by coordinate cutoffs and the off-diagonal smoothing condition. The only worked example is the operator \(d+d^*\), its Laplacian, and the Hodge identification with de Rham cohomology. The final timetable is administrative, not another mathematical result.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Enveloping-algebra construction of radial differential operators
summary: The second Harish-Chandra lecture constructs \(\Gamma_y\), transferring differentiation in the conjugating variable to the section. Its associated-graded calculation yields a PBW decomposition and the constant transverse term defining the radial operator. The first part of P000195 still belongs to this lecture; the dated 27 February heading starts record 122.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: Distributional descent and the induction step for regularity
summary: The third lecture returns to continuous fiber integration, pulls an invariant distribution back to \(G\times\Xi'\), and factors it as Haar measure times a distribution on the centralizer. It states intertwining with radial differential operators and finite central codimension, thereby reducing local integrability to a smaller group. The notebook itself rejects an attempted explicit inverse-substitution formula.

speaker: A. A. Kirillov
title: The Lorentzian rank-one model for invariant regularity
summary: A short final Kirillov note isolates the form \(x^2+y^2-z^2\), its wave operator, and invariant distributions annihilated by a polynomial in that operator. The question of local summability is the rank-one Lie-algebra case of the theorem developed in the preceding lectures. Arnold's report begins later on the same page.

speaker: V. I. Arnold
title: Surface diffeomorphism groups; adjacent Anosov note on operator Fourier transformation
summary: Arnold reports Earle--Eells on the topology of the identity component of the diffeomorphism group of an oriented surface, with genus-by-genus answers and the quasiconformal proof strategy. P000199 begins a distinct, explicit \ru{Аносов} heading and develops an operator-valued Fourier transform attributed to Maslov. The catalogue supplies no separate record for this subsection; its three items are retained here with Anosov as the item-level speaker. This grouping preserves source coverage without attributing Anosov's mathematics to Arnold.

speaker: A. N. Parshin
title: Algebraic group actions and geometric orbit quotients
summary: Parshin's report on Mumford defines a regular algebraic action and asks when its orbit set carries an algebraic quotient structure. It records stabilizer semicontinuity, necessary restrictions on a morphism whose fibers are individual orbits, and the affine reductive closed-orbit criterion in compressed form. An unlabelled hyperbola-like sketch cannot be uniquely identified. The later projective continuation, record 128, preserves only a heading.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Stable symbols and an axiomatic index
summary: Dynin's second lecture defines compactly supported stable symbols and lists homotopy invariance, additivity, products, excision, vanishing for symbols from the base, and the one-dimensional winding normalization. The first isolated uniqueness claim mentions only the first two properties and is false literally; the later full family of axioms supplies the intended setting. This is related to the earlier index lectures, but no already-indexed open question is reasserted.

speaker: A. S. Dynin
title: Boundary systems with varying partial indices and global completion
summary: The March 27 material begins below the separate March 20 Parshin heading on P000202. The catalogue attributes this record to Dynin, but the manuscript names Eskin on P000203; this could introduce Eskin's work or a further speaker, and the catalogue attribution is retained with that qualification. The lecture treats a continuous family of normal half-line problems even when individual partial indices jump, auxiliary potentials and boundary equations, localization, and a global completion question. The latter matches the framework and criterion of Vishik--Eskin's paper received 27 April 1967, rather than merely a later paper on the same subject.

speaker: A. N. Parshin
title: Projective varieties: heading of the continued Mumford report
summary: Only the handwritten date 20 March and the headings ``Continuation of Parshin's report'' and ``The case of projective varieties'' survive. The next visible mathematics is below a new date, 27 March, and concerns matrix factorization; it belongs to record 127. No theorem from Mumford's projective invariant theory is supplied by this heading. Catalogue source order is preserved even though record 128 has the earlier date.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Petrovsky lacunas and Atiyah’s algebraic-geometric formulation
summary: S. Gelfand explicitly reports Atiyah's Bourbaki expos\'e 319, delivered in February 1967 and printed in 1968. The notes define strict hyperbolicity, the retarded fundamental solution and stable lacunas, construct the two Petrovsky homology classes, state the even-order/even-dimension criteria, and begin the residue-integral proof. The shift from \(\mathbb R^n\) to coordinates \(x_0,\ldots,x_n\) is resolved by writing \(N=n+1\). Empty real and complex sections, projective orientation choices, and twisted canonical forms must be distinguished. The notes stop at the Herglotz--Petrovsky formula; later algebraic de Rham proof details are not attributed to the seminar.
